purpose: Independent practice of B2.8 (numerator as repeated addition).
student_learning_goal: I can show that 3/4 = 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 and 4 × 1/2 = 2 wholes using fraction strips.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can show that 3/4 = 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 and 4 × 1/2 = 2 wholes using fraction strips.
header.character_watermark: Tony the Toolkit Master in the top-right corner. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Write each fraction as repeated addition AND as multiplication.
parts.visual_layout: Top of the page. Six fraction-decomposition rows.

image_placeholders.description: Six fraction decomposition rows in B&W line-art, stacked vertically. Each ~7in × 0.7in. Format: fraction on left (e.g., 3/4), addition slot ('___+___+___'), multiplication slot ('___×___'). Fractions: 3/4, 5/6, 7/8, 4/5, 3/10, 5/8.
image_placeholders.placement: Top of the page; six rows.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P1_DECOMP: keywords (fraction, decomposition) name what the rows ask for.

parts.student_instructions: Solve each. Identify which give whole numbers.
parts.visual_layout: Middle. Six multiplication problems in a 2x3 grid.

image_placeholders.description: Six multiplication problems in B&W line-art, 2-row × 3-column grid. Each ~2.5in × 1.5in. Pre-fills: 4×1/3, 5×1/4, 6×1/2, 8×1/4, 7×1/3, 3×1/5. Below each: result line and 'Whole number? Y/N' bubble.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P2_FRAC_MULT: keywords (multiplication, fractions) name what the boxes ask for.

parts.student_instructions: Pick a fraction. Write it 3 different ways: as a fraction, as repeated addition, as multiplication.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. A blank box.

image_placeholders.description: A blank rectangular box in B&W line-art, ~7in × 2in, with light-grey solid outline. Tony thinking-bubble icon in the top-right corner.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P3_THREE_WAYS_BOX: keywords (three-ways, fraction) name what the box asks for.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, find another multiplication that gives a whole-number result.
teacher_notes: Lesson 4 consolidation. Use Part 2's whole-number identification as evidence of mastery. Watch for Part 2 children who collapse 1/4 to 1.
